Suppose X has an order such that every subset which is bounded above has a least upper bound. (For example, the real numbers or any finite type, but not the rationals.) Is there a standard term for this property of X? And does mathlib have this property?

(This comes up when defining the support function of a polyhedron/(convex) set, but I'm sure this must be an established term elsewhere.)
I don't think all finite sets satisfy this property
we have docs#ConditionallyCompletePartialOrderSup for bounded above directed sets having a least upper bound

Ah, that's close. At first, I was confused by the SupSet hypotheses (e.g., not every subset of real numbers has a supremum) --- but then realized that the definition of suprema can have a junk value for unbounded sets. So, this could fit my bill, thanks!
Indeed, SupSet is just a notation class like Add; it furnishes a "supremum" operator but doesn't place any restrictions at all on its properties, so it isn't really a "hypothesis" as such.
technically it is adding the hypothesis that your type is nonempty
